intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

selected_hotel.name: Þingvellir National Park, Golden Circle Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the spectacular Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and the tour includes hot chocolate and photography tips to capture the lights.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy the outdoor lagoon surrounded by lava fields, use the complimentary silica mud mask, and unwind in one of Iceland's most iconic natural hot spring experiences.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geothermal activity, bubbling geysers, and stunning countryside scenery. A more authentic and less crowded alternative to the Blue Lagoon with equally soothing mineral-rich waters.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant culinary scene and cultural landmarks on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup, and fresh seafood, while visiting iconic spots like Hallgrímskirkja church, the colorful old harbor, and local artisan markets.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's breathtaking multicolored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a soak in natural geothermal hot springs at Landmannalaugar. The surreal landscape of steaming vents, obsidian lava fields, and vivid mineral-streaked mountains makes this an unforgettable combination of hiking and hot spring bathing.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Þingvellir National Park, Golden Circle Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for arrival.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and pick up a pre-booked budget rental car (essential for Iceland travel). Stop at a Bonus or Krónan supermarket near Reykjavík to stock up on groceries and snacks for the trip — this is key to keeping costs low. Drive approximately 1.5 hours northeast toward Þingvellir National Park.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to Þingvellir National Park / Golden Circle Boutique Stay. After settling in, wrap up warm and take a short walk around the immediate area to orient yourself. If skies are clear, step outside after dark for your first chance to spot the Northern Lights — January offers up to 18+ hours of darkness, maximizing aurora viewing opportunities. Download the Icelandic Met Office Aurora Forecast app to track activity.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport arrivals hall.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget meal at the airport — a hot dog from a kiosk (~600 ISK) or a sandwich from a convenience store.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the accommodation using groceries purchased at the supermarket (pasta, canned goods, eggs). Budget: ~1,500 ISK per person.

day_by_day.notes: January days are very short in Iceland — expect only 4–5 hours of daylight (roughly 11:00–15:30). Temperatures can be -5°C to 5°C. Pack layers, waterproofs, and thermal base layers. Aurora activity is possible any clear night — always check the forecast before bed.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, drive to Þingvellir National Park (just minutes from the accommodation). Walk the Almannagjá Gorge — a dramatic rift valley where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. This is free to enter. Explore the historic site of the Alþingi (Iceland's ancient parliament) and enjoy the stunning frozen winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive along the Golden Circle route to Geysir Geothermal Area (~45 min from Þingvellir). Watch the famous Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting water 20–30 meters into the air. Entry to the geothermal area is free. Browse the visitor center to warm up without purchasing anything.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Gullfoss Waterfall (~10 min from Geysir) — one of Iceland's most iconic waterfalls. In January it may be partially frozen, making it even more spectacular. Return to accommodation before dark. Spend the evening watching for Northern Lights from outside the guesthouse — check the aurora forecast and set an alarm for peak activity hours (often midnight–2am).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — oats, toast, eggs. Budget: ~500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from accommodation — sandwiches, fruit, thermos of hot coffee/tea. Budget: ~600 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner at accommodation — soup, bread, and cheese. Budget: ~1,200 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Þingvellir, Geysir, and Gullfoss are the three pillars of the Golden Circle and are all free or very low cost to visit. Wear ice cleats (available at most Icelandic hardware or outdoor stores for ~2,000 ISK) as paths can be icy in January. Gullfoss parking is free.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir, about 45 minutes from Þingvellir. This is one of Iceland's most affordable natural hot spring pools (~3,000 ISK entry vs. ~8,000+ ISK for the Blue Lagoon). Soak in the geothermally heated pool surrounded by a snowy winter landscape — a magical budget-friendly hot spring experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward the Þingvellir area and explore the Kerið Volcanic Crater (~700 ISK entry fee). Walk the rim of this vivid red and green crater lake — in winter it may be partially frozen and dusted with snow. Afterward, stop at Laugarvatn village and walk along the shores of Laugarvatn lake, where natural hot springs bubble up from the ground along the beach (free).
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation and cook dinner. If skies are clear, this is a prime Northern Lights night — set up outside with a warm blanket and thermos. The area around Þingvellir is one of Iceland's best aurora viewing spots due to minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — yogurt, skyr (Icelandic dairy, cheap and filling), granola. Budget: ~500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten in the car or at the Secret Lagoon café area (bring your own food). Budget: ~600 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered — pan-fried fish (cod or haddock from supermarket), potatoes, and vegetables. Budget: ~1,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is best visited early morning to avoid crowds. Bring your own towel if possible (rental adds cost). Flúðir is a tiny village — there are no budget restaurants, so self-catering is ideal here.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south toward the South Coast (approximately 1.5–2 hours from Þingvellir). First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — a stunning cascade that you can walk behind in summer, though the path may be icy/closed in January. Entry and parking are free (parking machine: ~750 ISK). Admire from the front and surrounding viewpoints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue 10 minutes east to Skógafoss Waterfall — one of Iceland's largest and most dramatic falls. Climb the 370 steps to the top for panoramic views of the South Coast. Free entry. Afterward, drive to the black sand beach at Reynisfjara near Vík (~45 min). See the dramatic basalt columns, sea stacks (Reynisdrangar), and powerful Atlantic waves. Free entry — but heed warning signs about sneaker waves.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the Þingvellir area (approximately 2 hours) or find a safe roadside pull-off on the South Coast to watch for Northern Lights over the black sand beaches and mountains — a truly unforgettable setting. Return to accommodation for dinner and rest.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — eggs, toast, coffee. Budget: ~500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Skógafoss or Reynisfjara. Budget: ~700 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered — lentil soup with crusty bread. Budget: ~1,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~4–5 hours total). Start early to maximize the limited daylight. Roads on the South Coast are generally well-maintained but check road.is before departing. Reynisfjara waves are extremely dangerous — never turn your back on the ocean.

day_by_day.morning: Take a leisurely morning at the accommodation. Relax and recover from the previous day's long drive. Use the time to plan the week ahead, check weather and aurora forecasts, and do any laundry if facilities are available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Reykjavík (approximately 45 minutes from Þingvellir). Explore the city on foot — walk along Laugavegur street (main shopping street), visit Hallgrímskirkja Church (exterior is free; tower entry ~1,000 ISK), and stroll down to the Old Harbour area. Visit the Harpa Concert Hall exterior for free and admire the stunning glass facade.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavík's free cultural offerings — the Sun Voyager sculpture by the waterfront is beautifully lit at night. Browse the colorful streets of the city center. Grab a budget dinner before heading back to Þingvellir.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered. Budget: ~500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Reykjavík hot dog from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — Iceland's most famous hot dog stand, ~500 ISK each. A true Icelandic budget institution.
meals.dinner: Grab a budget meal in Reykjavík — Hlöllabátar (submarine sandwiches) or Noodle Station (Asian noodle soup, ~1,800–2,200 ISK) are popular affordable options.

day_by_day.notes: Reykjavík is expensive by global standards, so limit shopping and stick to free sights. The Hallgrímskirkja tower offers great views but the exterior and surrounding neighborhood are equally impressive for free. Parking in Reykjavík can be costly — use park-and-ride options or free street parking outside the city center.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Reykjadalur Hot Spring Thermal River near Hveragerði (~30 min from Þingvellir). Hike approximately 3km up into the valley to reach a geothermally heated river where you can bathe for free. The hike takes about 45–60 minutes each way through a steaming geothermal landscape — absolutely stunning in winter snow. Completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: After returning from the hike, dry off and warm up in the car. Drive into Hveragerði town and explore the greenhouse village — geothermal energy heats greenhouses year-round. The Hveragerði Geothermal Park in town has bubbling hot springs and mud pools (small entry fee or viewable from the street).
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation. This is a great evening for aurora hunting — the area around Þingvellir lake offers dark skies and reflective water for stunning aurora photography. Set an alarm for midnight if the KP index is 3 or above.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — pack a hearty breakfast before the hike. Budget: ~600 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the hot spring river (waterproof bag recommended). Budget: ~700 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered — hearty stew with lamb (affordable at Icelandic supermarkets). Budget: ~1,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: The Reykjadalur hike is one of Iceland's best free experiences. Wear waterproof boots and bring a swimsuit and towel. The trail can be icy — use crampons. Water temperature varies along the river — test before submerging. This is a moderately strenuous hike (~6km round trip) with 200m elevation gain.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Langjökull Glacier area (~1.5 hours from Þingvellir). Stop at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls near Borgarnes — these are stunning and free to visit. Hraunfossar features dozens of small springs emerging from a lava field directly into a river, and in winter the surrounding landscape is snow-covered and magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Deildartunguhver hot spring near Reykholt — the highest-flow hot spring in Europe, with boiling water gushing from the ground at 180 liters per second. Free to view from the designated area. Stop at the Krauma Geothermal Baths nearby (~3,500 ISK) — a smaller, more affordable alternative to the Blue Lagoon with naturally heated pools.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Þingvellir (approximately 1.5 hours). Quiet evening at the accommodation with dinner. Check aurora forecast — the drive back through the highlands may offer excellent aurora viewing opportunities away from any light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered. Budget: ~500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in the car or at Hraunfossar. Budget: ~700 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered — pasta with tuna and vegetables. Budget: ~1,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Krauma Geothermal Baths are a great budget alternative to the Blue Lagoon — smaller, less crowded, and significantly cheaper. Book in advance online. Roads in the Borgarnes/Reykholt area are generally good but check road.is. This is a long day — approximately 3+ hours of driving total.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day at or near the accommodation. Sleep in and recover from the week's activities. Take a slow morning walk around Þingvellir National Park — the park is free and the winter silence is extraordinary. Walk along the Öxará River and explore the historic church (Þingvallakirkja) and old farmstead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Laugarvatn Fontana Geothermal Baths (~20 minutes from Þingvellir). These lakeside baths are more affordable than the Blue Lagoon (~3,500 ISK) and feature natural steam rooms built over geothermal vents on the lake shore. Soak and relax with views of Laugarvatn lake.
day_by_day.evening: Return to accommodation for a relaxed evening. Cook a special dinner to celebrate the halfway point of the trip. If skies are clear, dedicate the full evening to Northern Lights watching — bring a chair, sleeping bag, and hot drinks outside.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — a lazy, indulgent breakfast. Skyr with honey, toast, fruit. Budget: ~600 ISK.
meals.lunch: Self-catered packed lunch or eat at the Laugarvatn Fontana café (soup of the day is usually affordable ~1,500–2,000 ISK).
meals.dinner: Self-catered — treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal: Icelandic lamb chops or salmon from the supermarket. Budget: ~2,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Laugarvatn Fontana also offers a unique geothermal bread baking experience — bread baked underground in the hot sand. The bread tasting is sometimes included with entry or available cheaply. January is peak aurora season — on a clear night with KP3+, the Þingvellir lake area offers world-class aurora viewing.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approximately 2.5 hours from Þingvellir). This is a long but spectacular drive. First stop: Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier volcano made famous by Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Walk along the Djúpalónssandur black pebble beach and see the rusted shipwreck remains. Free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Arnarstapi and Hellnar coastal area — dramatic lava arch formations, sea cliffs, and bird colonies (though most birds will have migrated in January). Walk the free coastal path between the two villages (~2.5km). Visit Vatnshellir Lava Tube Cave if budget allows (~2,500 ISK with a guided tour — highly recommended).
day_by_day.evening: Find accommodation in the Snæfellsnes area for the night if budget allows (guesthouse or hostel ~6,000–9,000 ISK) OR drive back toward Þingvellir (2.5 hours). If staying, the peninsula's dark skies offer exceptional Northern Lights viewing over the glacier.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before departure. Budget: ~500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Djúpalónssandur beach. Budget: ~700 ISK.
meals.dinner: If staying on the peninsula: Fjöruhúsið café in Hellnar is a cozy option (~2,500–3,500 ISK for a meal). If returning to Þingvellir: self-catered dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes is often called 'Iceland in miniature' — it has glaciers, lava fields, fishing villages, hot springs, and dramatic coastlines all in one peninsula. This is the longest driving day of the trip. Check road conditions carefully — the peninsula road can be challenging in winter. Consider this an optional overnight extension.

day_by_day.morning: If overnight on Snæfellsnes: explore Grundarfjörður village and the iconic Kirkjufell mountain — the most photographed mountain in Iceland, and especially dramatic in winter. Walk to the Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall beside it (free). If returned to Þingvellir: morning hike in the national park along the Lögberg (Law Rock) trail.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back to the Þingvellir/Golden Circle area if on Snæfellsnes (2.5 hours). Stop at Borgarnes Settlement Center on the way — the exterior and town are free to explore. Alternatively, revisit the Geysir area in the afternoon to see Strokkur erupt again in different light conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at accommodation. Organize gear, charge camera batteries, and prepare for the final days. Aurora watch from the accommodation grounds — set a midnight alarm if forecast is favorable.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered or hostel breakfast if on Snæfellsnes. Budget: ~500–800 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch in the car during the drive back. Budget: ~700 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at Þingvellir accommodation. Budget: ~1,200 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Kirkjufell is most dramatic in winter with snow on its distinctive pyramid shape. The waterfall beside it can be partially frozen in January, creating incredible ice formations. If you missed the Northern Lights earlier in the trip, tonight and the remaining nights are your final chances — January KP forecasts are your best friend.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Westman Islands (Vestmannaeyjar) — take the Herjólfur ferry from Landeyjahöfn (~40 min from Þingvellir). Ferry costs approximately 2,800 ISK each way. The islands feature dramatic volcanic landscapes including Eldfell volcano (1973 eruption) and Helgafell. Walk up Eldfell for panoramic views — free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Heimaey town on the Westman Islands — walk through the area where lava buried houses in 1973, visit the Eldheimar Museum (Pompeii of the North) if budget allows (~2,000 ISK), or view the exterior and read information boards for free. Walk along the harbor and see the puffin cliffs (puffins are gone in January but the cliffs are dramatic).
day_by_day.evening: Take the evening ferry back to the mainland. Return to Þingvellir accommodation. The ferry crossing offers a chance to spot marine life and seabirds even in January.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before departure. Budget: ~500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Grab a budget meal in Heimaey town — the local bakery (Lundinn) offers affordable sandwiches and pastries (~1,000–1,500 ISK).
meals.dinner: Self-catered back at accommodation. Budget: ~1,200 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance at herjolfur.is — winter schedules are reduced. The crossing can be rough in January — take seasickness medication if needed. Landeyjahöfn is approximately 40 minutes from Þingvellir via the Ring Road. The Westman Islands are a unique and often-overlooked destination that most tourists miss.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — revisit your favorite spots from the trip. Return to Þingvellir National Park for a longer hike — the Háabrún trail offers views over the entire rift valley and Þingvallavatn lake (Iceland's largest natural lake). The park is completely free and stunning in all weather conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Nesjavellir Geothermal Power Plant (~20 minutes from Þingvellir). The exterior is viewable for free and the steaming pipes and towers against the mountain backdrop are dramatic and photogenic. Alternatively, revisit the Secret Lagoon for a final hot spring soak to celebrate the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt — this is your last night. Drive to the darkest spot you can find away from any settlements (the Þingvellir highlands are perfect). Set up a camp chair, wrap in a sleeping bag, and spend 1–2 hours watching the skies. If the aurora appears, this will be the highlight of the entire trip. Return to accommodation for a celebratory self-catered dinner.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered — use up remaining groceries. Budget: ~500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the hike. Budget: ~700 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered celebration dinner — use up remaining food supplies and any Icelandic treats purchased during the trip. Budget: ~1,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Pack bags tonight and prepare for early departure tomorrow. Return the rental car with a full tank of petrol (fill up outside Reykjavík where prices are slightly lower). Double-check all accommodation checkouts and flight details. January 27 is your departure day.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of accommodation and drive to Keflavík International Airport (approximately 1 hour from Þingvellir). Return the rental car at the airport — allow extra time for this process. Check in for departure flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. If time allows before the flight, browse the duty-free shop at the airport — Icelandic chocolate (Nói Síríus), lamb jerky, and Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps) make great budget-friendly souvenirs. Duty-free prices are significantly lower than in-town shops.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight — reflect on 13 incredible days in Iceland. Review your Northern Lights photos, hot spring memories, and the dramatic volcanic landscapes of this extraordinary country.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before checkout or grab a coffee and pastry at a Keflavík petrol station (~800–1,000 ISK).
meals.lunch: Airport café or bring remaining packed snacks from the accommodation.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for car return, check-in, and security at Keflavík. The airport is about 50km from Reykjavík — factor in driving time from Þingvellir (approximately 1 hour total). Keflavík can be very windy — flights are rarely cancelled but can be delayed. Total estimated trip budget (excluding flights and accommodation): approximately 80,000–110,000 ISK (~€550–€750) for 13 days, covering car rental, fuel, food (mostly self-catered), and paid attractions.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Þingvellir National Park, Golden Circle Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the spectacular Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and the tour includes hot chocolate and photography tips to capture the lights.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Keflavík International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, pick up pre-booked rental car (4WD strongly recommended for January), and grab a coffee at the airport café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Keflavík to Þingvellir National Park (~1.5 hours via Route 1 and Route 36). Check in to Golden Circle Boutique Stay. Take a short orientation walk around the hotel grounds and nearby lakeshore of Þingvallavatn to acclimate and stretch your legs after the flight.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into your room, then head out for your first Northern Lights watch from the hotel grounds or a nearby dark-sky spot along the lake. January offers long dark nights — lights out by 17:00 means excellent aurora hours. Keep the Visit Iceland aurora forecast app open.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or airport café at Keflavík
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or soup at Kaffi Duus near Keflavík or a roadside petrol station (N1/Orkan) on the drive — budget ~1,500–2,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Dinner at Þingvellir Visitor Centre restaurant or the hotel's own dining room if available — expect hearty Icelandic lamb soup or fish of the day, ~3,500–5,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January sunset is around 16:00–17:00. Drive carefully on potentially icy Route 36. Stock up on snacks and water at a supermarket (Krónan or Bónus) near Selfoss if passing through. Aurora KP index: check en.vedur.is nightly.

day_by_day.morning: Þingvellir National Park morning exploration — walk the Almannagjá canyon (the rift valley between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates). Visit the historic Lögberg (Law Rock) and Öxará River. Dress in full winter layers; trails may be icy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the Golden Circle loop (~30 min from Þingvellir): Visit Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes. Explore the surrounding hot spring fields and fumaroles. Stop at the Geysir Center gift shop to warm up.
day_by_day.evening: Continue to Gullfoss Waterfall (20 min from Geysir). Experience the dramatic two-tiered falls partially frozen in January. Return to hotel. Evening Northern Lights hunt from a dark field near the hotel — ask staff for the best local spots.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or self-catered at the room — yogurt, skyr, bread (~included or ~1,500 ISK)
meals.lunch: Lindin Restaurant near Þingvellir or packed lunch from hotel — soup and bread ~2,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant near Geysir (tomato soup, pizza, fresh produce grown on-site) — ~4,500–6,000 ISK, book ahead

day_by_day.notes: Friðheimar is very popular — reserve a table 24–48 hours in advance. Gullfoss can be extremely windy in January; wear a balaclava and windproof jacket. Total driving today ~80 km.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir (~40 min from Þingvellir) — Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring pool at ~38–40°C. Soak and relax in the geothermal waters surrounded by steaming vents and a small geyser.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Kerið Volcanic Crater Lake (~25 min from Flúðir). Walk the rim of this striking red-and-black caldera with a vivid blue-green lake below. Return toward Þingvellir via the scenic Route 35.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening at the hotel. Enjoy the hotel's hot tub or geothermal pool if available. Keep aurora alerts active — clear January nights at Þingvellir offer spectacular views away from city light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Café at the Secret Lagoon or packed lunch — soup and coffee ~2,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant or self-catered dinner with groceries — lamb stew or skyr parfait ~3,000–4,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon entry fee ~3,200 ISK per adult (book online). Kerið entry fee ~700 ISK. Path around Kerið can be icy — use microspikes if available. Total driving ~90 km.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip toward Reykjavik (~45 min drive). Morning visit to the National Museum of Iceland (Þjóðminjasafn) — excellent exhibits on Viking settlement and Icelandic history. Open 10:00–17:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk Reykjavik's colourful old town: Hallgrímskirkja church (take the tower elevator for panoramic views), Tjörnin pond, and Laugavegur shopping street. Browse local wool shops for lopapeysa sweaters.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — join a guided minibus tour departing from Reykjavik into the wilderness away from light pollution. Tours typically run 21:00–00:00 and guarantee a second free trip if lights don't appear. Return to hotel after.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic rye bread with smoked lamb or herring ~2,500–3,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn (The Sea Baron) in Reykjavik harbour — famous lobster soup and grilled fish skewers ~3,500–4,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Northern Lights tour cost ~9,000–12,000 ISK per person — book online in advance. Museum entry ~2,500 ISK. Hallgrímskirkja tower ~1,000 ISK. Drive back to Þingvellir after the tour (~45 min, check road conditions at road.is).

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely morning — sleep in after late aurora tour. Late breakfast at hotel. Take a gentle snowshoe or winter walk along the shores of Þingvallavatn lake (the largest natural lake in Iceland). Look for Arctic char under the ice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Silfra Fissure in Þingvellir National Park — book a snorkelling or dry-suit diving tour between the tectonic plates in crystal-clear glacial water (visibility up to 100m). One of the most unique experiences in Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: Warm up back at the hotel with a hot shower and cosy dinner. Optional: self-guided stargazing and aurora watch from the hotel garden with a thermos of hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Late hotel breakfast or self-catered skyr with granola
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or light café stop near the park visitor centre ~1,500–2,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant — pan-fried Arctic char with potatoes and butter sauce ~4,000–5,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Silfra snorkelling tour ~19,000–25,000 ISK — book well in advance as it's extremely popular. Water temperature is ~2–4°C year-round; dry suits are provided. Not suitable if you're sensitive to cold. Minimum age/health requirements apply.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south toward the South Coast (~1.5–2 hours from Þingvellir via Route 1). First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall — walk behind the curtain of water (may be icy in January, check conditions). Then visit nearby Gljúfrabúi hidden canyon waterfall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skógafoss Waterfall — climb the 527 steps to the top for sweeping views across the coastal plain. Visit the nearby Skógar Folk Museum for insight into traditional Icelandic farm life.
day_by_day.evening: Check in at a guesthouse near Vík or Skógar for the night (pre-booked mid-range accommodation ~15,000–20,000 ISK). Dinner in Vík town. Evening aurora watch from Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach — dramatic basalt columns and sea stacks.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Þingvellir before departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at a petrol station N1 near Hvolsvöllur ~1,500–2,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík — lamb burger or fish and chips ~3,500–5,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: This is an overnight excursion away from your base hotel — confirm with Golden Circle Boutique Stay about luggage storage or flexible check-out. Reynisfjara beach has dangerous sneaker waves — never turn your back on the ocean. Total driving ~180 km.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach in daylight (~10:00 sunrise). Photograph the iconic Reynisdrangar sea stacks and basalt column cave Hálsanefshellir. Drive to Dyrhólaey promontory for panoramic coastal views (road may be closed — check).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (~2 hours east of Vík). Walk along the shore watching icebergs calve from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier and float through the lagoon. Visit Diamond Beach (Breiðamerkursandur) where ice chunks wash up on black sand.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back west toward Þingvellir base (~3.5 hours) or overnight near Skaftafell/Kirkjubæjarklaustur to break the journey. Aurora watch from the vast open plains of the south coast — minimal light pollution.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast near Vík
meals.lunch: Jökulsárlón Café (Glacier Lagoon visitor centre) — lamb soup or fish soup ~2,500–3,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Hótel Skaftafell restaurant or Systrakaffi in Kirkjubæjarklaustur ~4,000–5,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: January road conditions on Route 1 east of Vík can be challenging — check road.is before departure. Jökulsárlón is ~370 km from Reykjavik; plan ~4 hours driving each way if doing as a day trip. Consider splitting this into two nights away from base.

day_by_day.morning: Return drive to Þingvellir base (~3–4 hours depending on overnight location). Scenic drive back along Route 1 through lava fields and past Eyjafjallajökull glacier volcano.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at Golden Circle Boutique Stay. Rest and recharge. Optional: visit Þingvellir National Park visitor centre for a film about Iceland's geology and history.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel. Book a private Northern Lights wake-up call service if the hotel offers it — staff wake you when aurora activity is high. Soak in the hotel hot tub under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse or hotel breakfast on the road
meals.lunch: Petrol station stop or Kaffi Árós near Selfoss ~1,500–2,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant — slow-cooked lamb shank with root vegetables ~4,500–6,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Use this day as a recovery and recharge day after the long South Coast excursion. Do laundry at the hotel if facilities are available. Review remaining itinerary and confirm any bookings for Days 9–13.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to the Snæfellsnes Peninsula (~2 hours from Þingvellir via Route 1 and Route 54). Visit Snæfellsjökull National Park — the glacier-capped volcano immortalised in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Centre of the Earth'. Walk the Djúpalónssandur pebble beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue around the peninsula: Arnarstapi and Hellnar coastal cliffs with dramatic lava arch formations. Stop at Búðakirkja — the iconic black church in a lava field. Visit Ólafsvík or Grundarfjörður for a warming café stop.
day_by_day.evening: Stay overnight in Grundarfjörður or Stykkishólmur (mid-range guesthouse ~15,000 ISK). Evening aurora hunt from the peninsula's north coast — excellent dark skies and mountain backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Þingvellir before departure
meals.lunch: Fjöruhúsið Café at Hellnar — famous for fish soup and homemade cakes ~2,500–3,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Narfeyrarstofa in Stykkishólmur or Grundarfjörður Guesthouse restaurant — fresh scallops or cod ~4,500–6,000 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Snæfellsnes roads can be very icy in January — 4WD essential. The peninsula is often called 'Iceland in miniature' for its diverse landscapes. Total driving ~200 km. Book overnight accommodation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Morning in Stykkishólmur — explore the charming harbour town, visit the Norwegian House museum, and walk up Súgandisey island (connected by a causeway) for panoramic views over Breiðafjörður bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive back toward Þingvellir via Route 54 and Route 1 (~2.5 hours). Stop at Deildartunguhver Hot Spring near Borgarnes — Europe's highest-flow hot spring, with boiling water gushing at 180 litres per second. Visit Krauma Geothermal Baths nearby for a relaxing soak.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Golden Circle Boutique Stay. Quiet evening with aurora watch from the hotel grounds. Review photos from the trip so far.

meals.breakfast: Guesthouse breakfast in Stykkishólmur or Grundarfjörður
meals.lunch: Borgarnes Settlement Centre café — lamb soup and bread ~2,000–3,000 ISK
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant at Þingvellir ~3,500–5,000 ISK or self-catered groceries

day_by_day.notes: Krauma Geothermal Baths entry ~3,900 ISK — a quieter, less touristy alternative to the Blue Lagoon with natural spring water. Deildartunguhver is free to visit. Total driving ~180 km.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day Golden Circle deep dive — revisit Þingvellir National Park in the morning for the Öxará Gorge walk and the historic Þingvallakirkja church (one of Iceland's oldest). Explore sections of the park you haven't seen yet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Haukadalur Geothermal Valley area — visit Gamla Laugin (Secret Lagoon) again for a longer, more leisurely soak if you want to relax, or explore the geothermal landscape around Hveravellir on a short hike.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell Golden Circle dinner at a local restaurant. Final dedicated Northern Lights hunt — hire a local guide for a private aurora tour from Þingvellir for the best experience on your last full aurora-hunting night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Þingvellir — buy supplies from a local supermarket the evening before ~1,500 ISK
meals.dinner: Lindin Restaurant at Þingvellir or Efstidalur II Farm Restaurant near Laugarvatn — homemade ice cream, lamb, and farm-fresh food ~4,500–6,500 ISK

day_by_day.notes: Efstidalur II is a working dairy farm with a restaurant and is extremely popular — book ahead. Private aurora guide from Þingvellir ~15,000–20,000 ISK for 2–3 hours. This is your penultimate full day — maximise aurora chances.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Þingvellir — leisurely breakfast and a last walk through the rift valley at sunrise (~11:00 in January). Pack up and check out of the Golden Circle Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Blue Lagoon (~1 hour from Þingvellir via Route 36 and Route 41). Spend 2–3 hours soaking in the iconic milky-blue geothermal waters. Book the Comfort package (includes silica mud mask and algae mask) — ~11,990 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to a hotel near Keflavík or Reykjavik for the final night (~15,000–20,000 ISK). Farewell dinner in Reykjavik — splurge slightly on your last night in Iceland.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast at Golden Circle Boutique Stay
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon café or LAVA Restaurant inside the Blue Lagoon (~4,000–6,000 ISK — can be added to your lagoon booking)
meals.dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) in Reykjavik — Icelandic tasting menu with local lamb, fish, and game ~8,000–12,000 ISK — a special farewell splurge

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon must be booked well in advance — January slots sell out quickly. Bring flip-flops and a hair tie. Lockers and towels are included in the Comfort package. Check out of Golden Circle Boutique Stay by 11:00 or arrange late check-out.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Iceland. If your flight departs in the afternoon, take a short walk along Reykjavik's Sæbraut coastal path or visit the Sun Voyager (Sólfar) sculpture by the harbour. Visit a local bakery for a final skyr or cinnamon roll (snúður).
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Keflavík International Airport (~45 min from Reykjavik). Return rental car — allow at least 2–3 hours before departure for fuel top-up, car return, and airport security. Depart Iceland.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or at destination.

meals.breakfast: Brauð & Co. bakery in Reykjavik — famous for their cinnamon rolls and pastries ~1,000–1,500 ISK
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café at Keflavík — Icelandic fish and chips or lamb wrap ~2,500–3,500 ISK
meals.dinner: In-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Return rental car with a full tank — petrol stations are plentiful along Route 41 toward the airport. Allow extra time for icy road conditions. Pick up duty-free Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps) or Icelandic chocolate at the airport as souvenirs. Góða ferð — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Þingvellir National Park, Golden Circle Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunting Tour
experiences.description: Join a guided minibus tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from Reykjavik's light pollution to witness the spectacular Aurora Borealis. Expert guides use real-time forecasts to find the best viewing spots, and the tour includes hot chocolate and photography tips to capture the lights.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy the outdoor lagoon surrounded by lava fields, use the complimentary silica mud mask, and unwind in one of Iceland's most iconic natural hot spring experiences.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring
experiences.description: Relax in Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891 surrounded by geothermal activity, bubbling geysers, and stunning countryside scenery. A more authentic and less crowded alternative to the Blue Lagoon with equally soothing mineral-rich waters.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Reykjavik's vibrant culinary scene and cultural landmarks on a guided walking tour. Sample traditional Icelandic dishes like skyr, lamb soup, and fresh seafood, while visiting iconic spots like Hallgrímskirkja church, the colorful old harbor, and local artisan markets.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's breathtaking multicolored rhyolite mountains in the Highlands and reward yourself with a soak in natural geothermal hot springs at Landmannalaugar. The surreal landscape of steaming vents, obsidian lava fields, and vivid mineral-streaked mountains makes this an unforgettable combination of hiking and hot spring bathing.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00 at Keflavík International Airport
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Keflavík Airport to Þingvellir National Park (approx. 1.5 hrs). En route, stop at the iconic Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa for a premium late-afternoon soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters. Pre-book a Lava Premium package including silica mud mask, algae mask, and a welcome drink served in the lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Þingvellir National Park Golden Circle Boutique Stay. Check in, unpack, and settle into your luxury suite. If skies are clear, step outside for a first chance at spotting the Northern Lights directly from the property — January offers prime aurora season with up to 18–19 hours of darkness.

meals.breakfast: On board flight
meals.lunch: Light snacks and welcome sparkling wine at Blue Lagoon's in-water bar
meals.dinner: In-suite welcome dinner arranged by the boutique hotel — expect locally sourced lamb, skyr-based desserts, and Icelandic craft beers or a curated wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer with your luxury travel concierge. Blue Lagoon must be booked well in advance, especially for January. Pack layers for the outdoor soak — temperatures can be -5°C to 2°C in January. Keep phone charged for aurora alerts.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay. Then embark on a private guided exploration of Þingvellir National Park — walk the Almannagjá rift valley, the dramatic fissure where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet. Visit the historic Lögberg (Law Rock) and the crystal-clear waters of Öxará River. Dress in premium thermal gear.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive the Golden Circle route with a private chauffeur-guide. Visit the legendary Geysir Geothermal Area — watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–40 meters into the winter sky. Continue to the majestic Gullfoss waterfall, partially frozen in January for a dramatic ice-laced spectacle.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for a Northern Lights Hunting Tour departing at dusk (around 16:00 in January). Join a guided minibus tour into the wilderness away from light pollution, equipped with aurora forecasting apps and expert guides. Hot cocoa and Icelandic blankets provided.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic gourmet breakfast at the hotel — smoked salmon, skyr, rye bread, and fresh pastries
meals.lunch: Warm lamb soup and fresh-baked bread at Geysir Center's premium café (Gullfoss Kaffi or similar)
meals.dinner: Back at the boutique hotel — a three-course dinner featuring pan-seared Arctic char, root vegetable medley, and Icelandic dairy-based dessert with local berry compote

day_by_day.notes: January sunrise is around 11:00 and sunset around 15:30 — plan outdoor sightseeing accordingly. Northern lights tours typically run 21:00–01:00. Aurora activity is rated 1–9 (KP index); aim for KP3+ for best viewing. Dress in full thermal layers.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Secret Lagoon Natural Hot Spring in Flúðir (approx. 45 min from Þingvellir). Iceland's oldest swimming pool dating to 1891, surrounded by geothermal steam vents and bubbling hot pots. A far more intimate and authentic experience than the Blue Lagoon — soak in 38–40°C waters surrounded by snow-dusted landscape in near-darkness.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming village of Flúðir and visit local mushroom and tomato greenhouses powered entirely by geothermal energy — a fascinating insight into Iceland's sustainable living. Return to the hotel for a private wellness session: in-room massage or sauna if available at the boutique property.
day_by_day.evening: Stargazing and Northern Lights vigil from the hotel grounds. The boutique stay's remote location in Þingvellir National Park — a UNESCO World Heritage Site — offers near-zero light pollution. Wrap up in provided outdoor blankets with hot drinks from the hotel's night service.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast at the hotel with freshly baked Icelandic kleinur (twisted doughnuts) and strong Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Secret Lagoon's on-site café — warm soup, open sandwiches, and hot drinks
meals.dinner: Premium in-hotel dinner — slow-roasted reindeer or Icelandic lamb shank with roasted root vegetables and a glass of Icelandic birch schnapps or imported premium wine

day_by_day.notes: The Secret Lagoon is a must-book in advance. Wear a swimsuit under your clothes for easy changing. Flúðir is a small village — confirm café hours in advance for January. The hotel concierge can arrange in-room spa treatments with 24-hour notice.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided snowmobile or super-jeep excursion to Langjökull Glacier (approx. 1.5 hrs from Þingvellir). Drive across the second-largest glacier in Iceland with an expert guide, exploring the otherworldly white expanse. Optional: enter the man-made ice tunnel inside the glacier for a surreal underground experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return journey stops at Hraunfossar and Barnafoss waterfalls — two stunning natural wonders where water cascades over lava fields and through a narrow rocky gorge. In winter, ice formations frame the falls dramatically. Warm up with thermos coffee provided by your guide.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay. Enjoy a private aurora photography workshop hosted by a local photographer at the hotel — learn long-exposure techniques and how to capture the Northern Lights on camera, then head out to shoot if aurora activity permits.

meals.breakfast: Full hot breakfast at the hotel — eggs, Icelandic sausages, smoked lamb, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Packed premium picnic lunch prepared by the hotel — insulated containers with hot soup, sandwiches, and Icelandic chocolate
meals.dinner: Chef's tasting menu at the hotel or a nearby farm-to-table restaurant — five courses featuring seasonal Icelandic ingredients, paired with a curated wine flight

day_by_day.notes: Glacier excursions require full waterproof outerwear and sturdy boots — the hotel can arrange rental gear. Ice tunnel tours must be pre-booked. Aurora photography workshop should be arranged through the hotel concierge at least 2 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south toward the Reykjanes Peninsula for a unique geothermal landscape walk at Krýsuvík-Seltún — steaming sulfur vents, boiling mud pools, and vivid ochre-and-rust colored earth. A raw, primal volcanic experience with boardwalk paths for safe exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the coastal cliffs of Reykjanes and visit the Bridge Between Continents — a symbolic footbridge spanning the fissure between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates. Explore the Reykjanes Lighthouse area and dramatic lava coastline battered by Atlantic waves.
day_by_day.evening: Head into Reykjavik (approx. 50 min from Reykjanes) for the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour — a premium guided evening experience sampling Icelandic delicacies including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, lamb hot dogs, and craft spirits at curated stops across the city.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — smoked trout on rye, Icelandic dairy, fresh berries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a geothermal greenhouse restaurant near Krýsuvík — tomato soup and freshly baked bread
meals.dinner: Food walking tour serves as dinner — multiple tasting stops culminating in a sit-down dessert at a premium Reykjavik patisserie

day_by_day.notes: Dress in full windproof gear for Reykjanes coastal areas — January Atlantic winds can be intense. The food tour typically runs 3–4 hours in the evening; confirm exact timing with the operator. Arrange a private car to and from Reykjavik.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Reykjavik. Morning visit to the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church — take the elevator to the top for panoramic city and mountain views. Walk Skólavörðustígur street lined with independent boutiques and galleries. Visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Kjarvalsstaðir) for contemporary Icelandic art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Harpa Concert Hall — a stunning geometric glass structure on the harbor front. Walk the old harbor district, visiting the whale-watching pier and the Viking Maritime Museum. Browse the premium design shops along Laugavegur street for Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa) and luxury souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Fine dining experience at one of Reykjavik's top restaurants — Dill Restaurant (New Nordic cuisine, Michelin-recognized) or Óx (intimate 12-seat tasting menu). Return to Þingvellir by private transfer under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at Café Loki near Hallgrímskirkja — traditional Icelandic rye bread, smoked lamb, and skyr parfait
meals.lunch: Lunch at Grillmarkaðurinn (The Grill Market) — premium Icelandic beef and seafood in a stylish setting
meals.dinner: Tasting menu at Dill or Óx — 7–10 courses of avant-garde New Nordic cuisine with wine pairing (approx. 25,000–35,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Reserve Dill or Óx at least 2–3 months in advance — both are extremely popular. Hallgrímskirkja tower tickets can be purchased on arrival. Laugavegur shops may have reduced January hours — check in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early for the South Coast. Visit Seljalandsfoss waterfall — in January, the falls may be partially frozen and illuminated by the brief winter sun, creating a magical ice sculpture effect. Walk behind the curtain of water (if ice conditions allow) for a unique perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Skógafoss waterfall — one of Iceland's largest and most dramatic falls. Climb the 370 steps to the top for sweeping views over the snowfields. Nearby, visit the Skógar Folk Museum to explore traditional Icelandic turf houses and heritage artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Check in at a luxury South Coast accommodation (arrange a one-night stay at a premium guesthouse near Vík, such as Hotel Katla or similar). Northern Lights hunt from the black sand beaches of Reynisfjara — the dramatic basalt columns and sea stacks create an extraordinary aurora backdrop.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — packed to-go option if departing before 08:00
meals.lunch: Lunch at Skógar — warm lamb stew and fresh bread at the museum café or a nearby farm restaurant
meals.dinner: Dinner at the South Coast accommodation — locally sourced fish stew, lamb, and Icelandic dairy desserts with South Coast wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Road conditions on the South Coast in January can be challenging — ensure your private transfer uses a 4WD vehicle. Check Veður.is (Icelandic Met Office) for road and aurora forecasts each morning. Reynisfjara beach has dangerous sneaker waves — stay well back from the water's edge.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Reynisfjara black sand beach at dawn — experience the dramatic volcanic coastline, the iconic Reynisdrangar sea stacks, and Reynisfjall mountain. The winter light (arriving around 11:00) casts a golden glow over the black sands and crashing Atlantic waves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to the Jökulsárlón Glacier Lagoon (approx. 2.5 hrs from Vík) — one of Iceland's most spectacular natural wonders. Watch enormous blue icebergs calved from Breiðamerkurjökull glacier drift silently through the lagoon. Visit Diamond Beach directly across the road where ice chunks wash ashore on black sand.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset (around 16:00) at Diamond Beach, followed by a Northern Lights vigil at the glacier lagoon — auroras reflected in the still, dark water and illuminating floating icebergs create one of the most breathtaking spectacles in Iceland. Return to South Coast accommodation.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the South Coast hotel
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jökulsárlón area — Glacier Goose Café or a packed premium lunch from the hotel
meals.dinner: Return dinner at accommodation — pan-seared Arctic char with dill cream sauce, roasted potatoes, and skyr panna cotta for dessert

day_by_day.notes: Jökulsárlón is approximately 378 km from Reykjavik — a full day's drive. Boat tours on the lagoon are not available in January (frozen conditions), but the shoreline walk is spectacular. Ice can make roads slippery — studded tires are mandatory in Iceland from November to April.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning glacier hike on Vatnajökull — Europe's largest glacier — with a certified glacier guide. Crampons, ice axes, and harnesses provided. Walk across ancient blue ice, peer into crevasses, and experience the otherworldly silence of the ice cap. A truly once-in-a-lifetime premium adventure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Skaftafell Nature Reserve within Vatnajökull National Park. Hike to Svartifoss (Black Falls) — a stunning waterfall framed by dramatic dark basalt columns that inspired the design of Hallgrímskirkja church. The short trail (approx. 1.5 hrs return) is manageable in winter with proper footwear.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back west along the Ring Road. Stop at the charming town of Kirkjubæjarklaustur for a warm dinner. Continue to a luxury overnight stay near Vík or begin return to Þingvellir (approx. 3 hrs). Northern Lights watch en route if conditions allow — pull off the Ring Road at designated viewpoints.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast from the hotel before the glacier hike
meals.lunch: Hot soup and sandwiches at the Skaftafell Visitor Center café
meals.dinner: Dinner at Systrakaffi in Kirkjubæjarklaustur — a cozy local restaurant serving hearty Icelandic lamb and fish dishes with homemade bread

day_by_day.notes: Glacier hiking requires a minimum fitness level and appropriate waterproof clothing. The guide company provides all technical equipment. Book glacier tours at least 1 week in advance. Driving the Ring Road at night in January requires extreme caution — consider stopping overnight rather than a full return drive.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Þingvellir National Park area (if not already back). Rest morning — enjoy a slow breakfast, in-room spa treatment, or private sauna session at the boutique hotel. Use the morning to recharge after the intensive South Coast days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Landmannalaugar Highland Hot Springs experience (accessible in winter only by super-jeep with a specialist operator). Trek through Iceland's breathtaking multicolored rhyolite mountains — vivid greens, pinks, reds, and yellows — and reward yourself with a soak in the natural geothermal hot spring pool surrounded by snow-covered peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for a luxurious evening. Private candlelit dinner in your suite or in the hotel's private dining room — a special mid-trip celebration meal with premium Icelandic ingredients and a fine wine selection chosen by the hotel sommelier.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at the hotel — eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and freshly squeezed juice
meals.lunch: Hot packed lunch provided by the super-jeep operator — insulated flasks of soup and hearty sandwiches consumed at Landmannalaugar
meals.dinner: Private in-suite or dining room dinner — lobster bisque, pan-seared lamb tenderloin, and a premium Icelandic cheese board with local honey

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar in winter requires a specialized super-jeep tour — standard vehicles cannot access the area. Book well in advance as spots are limited. Bring a swimsuit and towel for the hot spring. The hike is moderate; inform your guide of any physical limitations.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided horse riding tour on Icelandic horses through the Þingvellir landscape. Icelandic horses are a unique breed known for their smooth tölt gait — perfect for beginners and experienced riders alike. Ride through snow-dusted lava fields and birch woodland in the pale winter light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Þingvellir National Park Visitor Center for an in-depth guided interpretation of the site's geological and historical significance — Iceland's original parliament (Alþingi) was established here in 930 AD. Walk the Hakið viewpoint trail for sweeping panoramic views over Lake Þingvallavatn.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunting Tour — second dedicated aurora tour of the trip with a different route into the wilderness. Expert guides use real-time aurora forecasting data to position the group optimally. Hot drinks and traditional Icelandic kleina pastries served under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — rye porridge with Icelandic berries, smoked fish selection, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Þingvellir National Park area café or a premium packed lunch from the hotel
meals.dinner: Dinner at a nearby Golden Circle premium restaurant — Friðheimar tomato farm restaurant (famous for tomato soup and fresh bread grown in geothermal greenhouses, with a unique ambiance)

day_by_day.notes: Horse riding tours typically last 1–2 hours. Helmets are provided; dress in windproof layers. Friðheimar restaurant is extremely popular — book well in advance. The restaurant operates in a working greenhouse, a unique dining experience. Northern lights tour departs around 21:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour over the Golden Circle and Þingvellir National Park — see the tectonic rift, Gullfoss, Geysir, and the vast Icelandic interior from the air. In clear conditions, views extend to Langjökull and Hekla volcanoes. A truly exclusive, bucket-list luxury experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relaxation afternoon at the boutique hotel. Optional: private snowshoeing excursion through the Þingvellir birch forest with a guide, or a curated in-room wellness experience with aromatherapy, hot stone massage, and a private hot tub session (if available at the property).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the hotel — a premium multi-course Icelandic feast arranged with the hotel chef. Celebrate the trip with champagne on arrival, a tasting menu of Iceland's finest ingredients, and a curated wine flight. Final Northern Lights vigil from the hotel terrace afterward.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast at the hotel — smoked salmon blinis, fresh fruit, and sparkling wine to mark the final full day
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the hotel — Icelandic fish cakes, salad, and skyr with Icelandic honey
meals.dinner: Farewell gala dinner — amuse-bouche, langoustine bisque, Icelandic lamb rack with herb crust, artisan cheese selection, and skyr soufflé with crowberry coulis

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours are weather-dependent — have a backup plan (extended spa day or additional Golden Circle drive). Book helicopter tours at least 1–2 weeks in advance through a premium operator such as Norðurflug or Icelands Helicopters. Farewell dinner should be arranged with the hotel 3–4 days in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely breakfast at the boutique stay. Pack and check out. Take a slow farewell walk through Þingvellir National Park — breathe in the crisp Icelandic air, take final photographs of the rift valley, and reflect on 13 extraordinary days.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Þingvellir to Keflavík International Airport (approx. 1.5 hrs). En route, optional final stop at the Blue Lagoon for a relaxing pre-flight soak — the Retreat Spa at the Blue Lagoon offers a premium in-water float experience ideal for a send-off. (Book the Retreat package for exclusive access.)
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Keflavík International Airport. Access the Saga Lounge or a premium airport lounge for final Icelandic refreshments before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Final full Icelandic breakfast at the hotel — a celebratory spread of all the favorites from the trip
meals.lunch: Blue Lagoon Lava Restaurant or in-lagoon refreshments — smoked salmon, Icelandic flatbread, and a farewell glass of sparkling wine
meals.dinner: Airport lounge or on board flight

day_by_day.notes: Check out time is typically 11:00 — confirm with the hotel. Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa requires advance booking and is a separate, more exclusive area from the main lagoon. Arrive at Keflavík Airport at least 2.5 hours before departure. Ensure all duty-free Icelandic spirits, chocolates, and lopapeysa sweaters are packed in checked luggage if purchased.

query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026
